reference_sql:
WITH both_rivals AS (
  SELECT product_id
  FROM competitor_prices
  WHERE competitor = 'Bliksem'
    AND observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01 00:00:00'
    AND observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00'
  INTERSECT
  SELECT product_id
  FROM competitor_prices
  WHERE competitor = 'Stroomhuis'
    AND observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01 00:00:00'
    AND observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00'
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products
FROM both_rivals
alternatives: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT b.product_id) AS products FROM competitor_prices b JOIN competitor_prices s ON s.product_id = b.product_id WHERE b.competitor = 'Bliksem' AND s.competitor = 'Stroomhuis' AND b.observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01 00:00:00' AND b.observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00' AND s.observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01 00:00:00' AND s.observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00'

WITH may_checks AS (SELECT product_id, competitor FROM competitor_prices WHERE observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01 00:00:00' AND observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00'), both_rivals AS (SELECT product_id FROM may_checks WHERE competitor = 'Bliksem' INTERSECT SELECT product_id FROM may_checks WHERE competitor = 'Stroomhuis') SELECT COUNT(*) AS products FROM both_rivals

other_way.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT b.product_id) AS products FROM competitor_prices b JOIN competitor_prices s ON s.product_id = b.product_id WHERE b.competitor = 'Bliksem' AND s.competitor = 'Stroomhuis' AND b.observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01 00:00:00' AND b.observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00' AND s.observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01 00:00:00' AND s.observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00'
other_way.tradeoff: A self-join with COUNT(DISTINCT ...) gives the same number, but it pairs every check with every other check before it counts.
